As Professor Shiffrin observes, however, cooperative endeavors 
(insurance, Social Security, public health) blur self regarding and other-
regarding 
behavior. Some in the community may be unwilling to 
subsidize what they consider bad choices by others. Here Professor 
Shiffrin 
suggests that to respect the autonomy 
of others in an 
interdependent society, it is necessary to accommodate some behavior 
one disagrees with. The challenge of unconscionability is the extent to 
which accommodation requires the enforcement of obnoxious promises. 
In her view, the type of autonomy associated with contracting is less 
central to one's sense of self than, say, the exercisr of conscience. On the 
other hand, the state has good cause not to further any disruption of "a 
rough resource equality of condition and fair treatment that we have 
fundamental commitments to maintaining." Consequently, there is a role 
for unconscionability even if one rejects paternalism. 
Seana Valentine 
Shiffrin, Paternalism, Unconscionability Doctrine, and Accommodation, 
29 Phil. & Pub. Affairs 205 (2000). 
Is Professor Shiffrin correct when she downplays the importance of 
contract 
in individual autonomy? And does her emphasis on self-
regarding behavior understate the challenges of determining just what 
that means when we apply it to the actions of the state? 
Price U nconscionability 
May a court determine that the price charged by a seller or supplier 
is so high that the contract is unconscionable on that ground alone? Must 
the court be prepared to say what the "intrinsic" value of the performance 
is? Must it be prepared to say would be a reasonable profit? The following 
case and notes suggest the parameters of answers to these questions. 
Stoll v. Xiong 
Court of Civil Appeals of Oklahoma, 2010. 
241 P.3d 301.

findmg_ a clause in his contract with Chong Lor Xiong and Mee Ya~g 
(collectively, Buyers) unconscionable. He contends the contract was valid 
and enforceable. We affirm the trial court's 
findings the contract 
paragraph supporting Stall's claim is unconscionable and Buyers were
